recipes.name: Củ Kiệu (Pickled Shallot Bulbs)
recipes.flavorProfile: Crunchy, sweet and sour, with a gentle allium bite.
recipes.healthBenefit: A crisp pickle that brings a little fiber; the brine is sweet.

ingredients.prepNote: roots and tops trimmed, outer skin peeled
1 tsp taken up by the bulbs, the rest for the soaking water, rinsed off
dissolved in the second soak to keep the bulbs crisp, rinsed off
ingredients.name: Alum (phèn chua)

ingredients.prepNote: 3 chilies, sliced

instructions: Trim the roots and tops of the bulbs and peel off the thin outer skin.
Dissolve the salt in enough water to cover the bulbs and soak them overnight, 8 to 10 hours, to take away the sharpness.
Drain, cover with fresh water, stir in the alum and soak for 2 hours more. Rinse well.
Spread the bulbs out and dry them in the sun for 1 to 2 days, until the skins are slightly wrinkled.
Boil the vinegar, sugar and water until the sugar dissolves, then let it cool completely.
Pack the bulbs and chili into clean, dry jars and pour the cooled brine over them to cover. Close the jars.
Leave 5 to 7 days before eating. One serving is 50 g.

nutritionHighlights.note: The brine sugar is counted in full.

citations.source: VTC News: Cách làm củ kiệu chua ngọt đơn giản

recipes.curationNote: VTC News, Cách làm củ kiệu chua ngọt đơn giản for every amount and step; 1 kg of bulbs; servings are not stated, so 50 g a serving is kept.

recipes.name: Tóp Mỡ (Pork Cracklings)
recipes.flavorProfile: Crisp, golden and rich, with a little salt.
recipes.healthBenefit: Mostly fat, used a spoonful at a time for crunch.

ingredients.cutPrep: what stays in the cracklings from 500 g pork fat, skin on, cut in pieces; the rest renders off as lard

ingredients.prepNote: a pinch

instructions: Rub the pork fat with the salt, rinse it clean and let it drain well.
Cook in an air fryer at 355°F (180°C) for 20 minutes, stirring now and then.
Raise to 390°F (200°C) for 15 minutes more, until the skin puffs and turns crisp. Pour off the rendered fat and keep it as lard.

citations.source: Cookpad Vietnam, Tóp mỡ da giòn rụm

recipes.curationNote: Cookpad Vietnam, Tóp mỡ da giòn rụm for every amount and step; 500 g pork fat with skin, 1 tsp salt rubbed on and rinsed off; air fryer 180°C 20 minutes, then 200°C 15 minutes until the skin puffs and crisps.

recipes.name: Chả Huế (Huế Peppered Pork Roll)
recipes.flavorProfile: Springy pork roll steamed in banana leaves, with plenty of cracked black pepper, garlic and fish sauce.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pork brings protein, thiamine and zinc; made with fatty pork and fish sauce, it is rich and salty.

ingredients.prepNote: with some fat, chilled until firm
tapioca starch
2 tbsp in the meat, a little more for the leaves
crushed
whole peppercorns, cracked

instructions: Put the ground pork in the freezer for about 2 hours, until firm but not frozen hard.
Mix the tapioca starch and baking powder into the water.
Process the pork, adding the starch water a little at a time, for about 15 minutes, until smooth and sticky.
Add 2 tablespoons of the oil, the fish sauce and the MSG and process again.
Crush the garlic and crack the peppercorns, then mix both into the pork until fragrant.
Rinse the banana leaves and dip them in hot water so they fold without tearing. Brush them lightly with the rest of the oil.
Wrap the pork tightly in the leaves and fold the ends to seal.
Steam for 20 minutes. It is done when a piece broken in half springs back. Cool, slice and keep in the fridge. One serving is about 50 g.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the fish sauce and MSG.

citations.source: Cookpad: Chả Huế gói lá chuối

recipes.curationNote: Cookpad, Chả Huế gói lá chuối for every amount and step; servings are not stated; the batch is about 880 g, so 17 servings of about 50 g.

recipes.name: Bánh Tráng Mè (Sesame Rice Crackers)
recipes.flavorProfile: Crisp and nutty, puffed over coals, with coconut, sesame and fried shallot.
recipes.healthBenefit: Sesame brings calcium, copper and healthy fats.

ingredients.prepNote: tapioca starch; the source gives 50 to 80 g
the source gives 600 to 700 ml
the frying oil is drained off and not counted
the source gives 30 to 40 g

instructions: Whisk the rice flour, tapioca starch, coconut milk, sugar, salt and pepper into a smooth batter, stir in the shredded coconut, sesame and fried shallots, and let it rest 30 minutes.
Heat a nonstick pan, pour in a layer 1 to 2 mm thick, cover and cook 1 to 2 minutes until set. Lift it onto a rack and repeat, stirring the batter each time.
Dry the rounds in the sun for 1 to 2 days, or in the oven at 175 to 195°F (80 to 90°C) until hard.
Toast over charcoal for 1 to 2 minutes, turning, or in an air fryer at 320 to 340°F (160 to 170°C) for 2 to 4 minutes, until puffed and crisp. Makes 15 to 20.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the rice flour and tapioca starch.

citations.source: Hoàng Hà Mobile, Bánh tráng dừa

recipes.curationNote: Hoàng Hà's bánh tráng dừa followed at the middle of each range it gives; it makes 15 to 20, counted as 18.

recipes.name: Mẻ (Fermented Rice)
recipes.flavorProfile: Sour and mild, used like a vinegar in fish and soups.
recipes.healthBenefit: A live ferment of rice and water; it adds sourness with almost no sugar or salt.

ingredients.baseName: Grains, rice, white, long-grain, regular, dry

ingredients.cutPrep: the rice rinsing water, boiled and cooled

instructions: Rinse the rice and keep the rinsing water. Cook the rice soft and let it cool.
Bring the rinsing water to a boil, let it cool, and pour it into a clean glass jar.
Add the cooked rice so the water covers it, seal the jar, and leave it at room temperature about 14 days, until the rice is sour, white and soft enough to mash.
Mash or sieve before using. One serving is 1 tablespoon.

citations.source: Điện máy Chợ Lớn, Cách làm và nuôi cơm mẻ

recipes.curationNote: Điện máy Chợ Lớn method 1 (500 g rice, 2 litres water) scaled to a fifth. 100 g rice cooks to about 20 tablespoons.

recipes.name: Bò Khô (Vietnamese Dried Beef)
recipes.flavorProfile: Chewy, sweet, spicy and garlicky, with five spice.
recipes.healthBenefit: Dense in protein and iron; also sweet and salty.

ingredients.cutPrep: sliced across the grain into bite-size pieces

ingredients.prepNote: 1 bulb, peeled and lightly smashed
8 tbsp
2 tbsp
1 tsp
2 tbsp; in place of mai quế lộ, a rose-scented sorghum liquor the database does not hold
1/4 tsp; in place of dark soy sauce, which the database does not hold
ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)

ingredients.prepNote: for frying the garlic and searing the beef
5 stalks, minced
5 chilies, chopped

instructions: Slice the beef across the grain into bite-size pieces. Mix it with the garlic, honey, oyster sauce, pepper, liquor, five-spice and soy sauce and leave for 2 hours.
Heat the oil in a pan and fry the garlic from the marinade until golden, then lift it out.
Sear the beef over high heat until golden on both sides and drain it on paper towels.
In a second pan, fry the lemongrass and chilies until fragrant. Add the fish sauce and sugar and stir well.
Add the beef and simmer on low heat until most of the liquid has cooked away and the sauce thickens. Stir in the fried garlic.
Spread the beef on a foil-lined rack and dry it in a 100 C (210 F) oven for 45 to 60 minutes, longer for drier beef.
Cool, cover and keep in the fridge. One serving is 30 g.

nutritionHighlights.note: A concentrated amount from the dried beef in each 30 g serving.
Beef supplies well absorbed heme iron.

recipes.curationNote: Cookpad, Bò khô cháy tỏi for every amount and step; servings are not stated; 1 kg of beef dries to about 600 g with its glaze (an estimate), so 20 servings of 30 g.

recipes.name: Ngó Sen Chua (Pickled Lotus Stems)
recipes.healthBenefit: A light, crunchy vegetable with fibre.

ingredients.cutPrep: young stems, peeled and cut in 5 cm lengths
ingredients.prepNote: stands in for young lotus stems (ngó sen), which no food database here lists
squeezed into the soaking water, which is poured off

ingredients.baseName: Pepper, hot chili, red or green
ingredients.prepNote: 1 chili
in the brine
the share taken up; the brine holds 200 ml
the share taken up; the brine holds 200 g
the share taken up; the brine holds 1/2 tsp

instructions: Peel the lotus stems, cut them in 5 cm lengths, and drop them straight into cold water with the juice of the 2 limes so they stay white. Drain.
Boil 200 ml water with 200 ml vinegar, 200 g sugar and 1/2 tsp salt until the sugar dissolves, then let it cool completely.
Pack the stems and sliced chili into a clean glass jar and pour in the cooled brine until they are fully covered.
Leave about 2 days at room temperature, then keep in the fridge and eat within about 1 month. About a quarter of the brine is eaten with the stems, so only that share is counted.

nutritionHighlights.note: Lotus stems are crisp and fibrous.

citations.source: FPT Shop, Ngó sen muối chua
Điện Máy Xanh, Cách làm ngó sen muối chua

recipes.curationNote: Both sources give the same brine for 500 g: 200 ml vinegar, 200 g sugar, 1/2 tsp salt, 200 ml water, 1 chili, 2 limes. One serving is 50 g.
